verdict.rationale: Terraform's apply docs describe a `-destroy` planning mode that "creates a plan to destroy all remote objects". Operations run in dependency order, which supports tearing down an entire environment through the plan/apply workflow. One community report notes that a single-run Kubernetes/Helm setup "doesn't handle cluster deletion well". That is an edge case in one provider setup, not a contradiction of the core capability. missing for 10: dedicated in-depth destroy command documentation in the pack, evidence of dependency-ordered or clean teardown specifically during destroy, independent hands-on corroboration of clean full-environment teardown.

support.subject: As a developer, I can tear down an entire environment cleanly with a destroy operation

citations.quote: These include `-destroy`, which creates a plan to destroy all remote objects
On approval, Terraform performs the proposed operations in the correct order, respecting any resource dependencies.
